# Spacer

Header: `winui/ui/panels/Spacer.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panels/Spacer.hpp`.

A gap in a stack that takes the room the other children leave. Built by [ui::Spacer](#uispacer).

A [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol) gives its children what they ask for along its axis and leaves the rest of its slot empty at the end. A spacer takes that rest instead, so the children after it are pushed to the far edge: a toolbar with its last button on the right is a horizontal stack with a spacer in front of that button. Several spacers share the room by their weight, together with the stack's fills ([FillControl](fill.md#uifillcontrol)). Outside a stack a spacer is an empty element of its minimum size.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  bar    = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
bar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Back"));
bar->add(std::make_unique<ui::SpacerControl>());
bar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Next"));
```

## `ui::Spacer`

A flexible gap in a stack: it takes the room the other children leave along the stack, which pushes whatever comes after it to the far edge. Builds a [ui::SpacerControl](#uispacercontrol).

A stack gives each child what it asks for and leaves the rest of its slot empty at the end. Put a [Spacer](#uispacer) where that empty room should be instead. With several spacers the room is shared by [`.weight`](#uispacer-weight), together with the stack's [ui::Fill](fill.md#uifill) children. Set a minimum gap with [`.min_width`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec), or [`.min_height`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec) in a vertical stack. The stack needs more room than its children ask for, or there is nothing to share. A stack sized to its content has none.

Example: 
```cpp
// A toolbar: two buttons on the left, one on the right.
window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing         = 8,
    .child_alignment = ui::Alignment::Center,
    .content         = {
        ui::Button{.text = "New"},
        ui::Button{.text = "Open"},
        ui::Spacer{},
        ui::Button{.text = "Settings"},
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Spacer{
    .weight, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uispacer-weight"></span>`weight` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{1.0f}` | This spacer's share of the leftover room, relative to the other spacers in the same stack. |
| <span id="uispacer-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uispacer-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uispacer-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uispacer-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uispacer-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uispacer-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uispacer-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Spacer>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

## `ui::SpacerControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A gap in a stack that takes the room the other children leave. Built by [ui::Spacer](#uispacer).

A [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol) gives its children what they ask for along its axis and leaves the rest of its slot empty at the end. A spacer takes that rest instead, so the children after it are pushed to the far edge: a toolbar with its last button on the right is a horizontal stack with a spacer in front of that button. Several spacers share the room by their weight, together with the stack's fills ([FillControl](fill.md#uifillcontrol)). Outside a stack a spacer is an empty element of its minimum size.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  bar    = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
bar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Back"));
bar->add(std::make_unique<ui::SpacerControl>());
bar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Next"));
```

### SpacerControl

```cpp
SpacerControl() = default
```

A spacer of weight 1.

### weight

```cpp
float weight() const
```

This spacer's share of the leftover room, relative to the other spacers in the same stack.

### set_weight

```cpp
void set_weight(float weight)
```

Sets the share; negative is treated as 0. Updates the layout.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

True: measuring reads nothing at all.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size, const MeasureContext&) const override
```

Nothing of its own: a spacer is as small as its minimum size until a stack stretches it.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer&, const RenderContext&) const override
```

Draws nothing.
